A day after two CJP leaders were remanded to judicial custody for two more days, former West Bengal Chief Minister Mamata Banerjee on Tuesday (October 20, 2026) accused the central authorities of perpetrating "state-sponsored terrorism" and "police-sponsored atrocities" and demanded their immediate release.
She also alleged that Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) co-convenors Ashutosh Ranka and Saurav Das were being subjected to torture.
In a post on X, Ms. Banerjee alleged that attempts were being made to extend the custody of the two and described the alleged treatment of young people as a "threat to democracy".
I can understand the desperate motive to extend the custody of Ashutosh and Saurav. This is a dangerous virus being used on a daily basis to attack democracy. Stop torturing the boys and girls of Gen Z. Those in power today, will not be in power tomorrow. From Kolkata to Delhi to Mumbai - throughout the country, atrocities have reached unprecedented levels. When our forefathers stood up to colonial rulers, they too had to face atrocities and yet they fought with conviction and valor. Let me say it clearly: this is state-sponsored terrorism. These are police-sponsored atrocities. These cannot sustain for long. When people with conviction keep standing up strongly for the cause, to Save India, to Save Democracy- only then will these arrogant and blindfolded politicians in government open their eyes. By that time the people would have won, and the murderers of democracy will be finished. If you believe in democracy, release Ashutosh and Saurav immediately.
"I can understand the desperate motive to extend the custody of Ashutosh and Saurav. This is a dangerous virus being used on a daily basis to attack democracy. Stop torturing the boys and girls of Gen Z," Ms. Banerjee said.
Mr. Ranka and Mr. Das were, on Monday (October 19), remanded to judicial custody for two more days after they were produced before a newly appointed special executive magistrate at the Mandir Marg police station in Delhi, an official said.
The two were initially sent to judicial custody for five days on October 13, after they allegedly climbed over a locked gate to enter Jantar Mantar, days after it was de-notified as a designated protest site. Along with other CJP activists, they displayed the national flag and raised slogans against Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar, before being detained.
ALSO WATCH CJP leaders Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka’s judicial custody extended by two days
Claiming that "atrocities had reached unprecedented levels" across the country, the Mamata All India Trinamool Congress supremo said the situation was not limited to any particular city.
"From Kolkata to Delhi to Mumbai - throughout the country, atrocities have reached unprecedented levels", she claimed.
Drawing a parallel with India's freedom struggle, Ms. Banerjee said those who fought against colonial rule had also faced atrocities but continued their struggle with conviction and courage.
"Let me say it clearly: this is state-sponsored terrorism. These are police-sponsored atrocities. These cannot sustain for long," she said.
Ms. Banerjee also alleged that people "protesting to protect democracy and the country would eventually prevail over those in power".
"When people with conviction keep standing up strongly for the cause to save India, to save democracy, only then will these arrogant and blindfolded politicians in government open their eyes," she said.
"If you believe in democracy, release Ashutosh and Saurav immediately," she added.
The CJP has alleged that the bail proceedings were deliberately delayed to prevent the release of its two co-convenors. It has also questioned the rejection of their bail sureties on what it described as vague grounds.
On Sunday (October 18), the special executive magistrate hearing their bail matter claimed that unidentified persons are threatening him, following which police registered a non-cognisable report.
Mr. Ranka and Mr. Das will be produced before the special executive magistrate again on Wednesday (October 21), sources said.
